A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same landmark-detection framework, renamed from CAMLD to CABLD. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, equations, and supplementary materials support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original landmark-detection results, component ablations, rotation robustness experiments, and supplementary contrast-augmentation examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds age-group analyses, neurological disease classification results, and a qualitative baseline comparison.

M1.justification: The CNN/center-of-mass detector, TPS alignment, consistency losses, adaptive loss weighting, and random-convolution augmentation are retained. CABLD is a renaming of CAMLD. The SVM classifiers in Section 4.6 evaluate downstream uses of its landmarks rather than revise the proposed detector.

E1.justification: Section 4.6 adds PPMI Parkinson's disease and healthy populations, ADNI Alzheimer's disease scans, biomarker comparisons, and PD/AD classification tasks. The original detector training datasets and four landmark-detection test datasets remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 and the rotation experiment retain their comparator membership and configurations. Supplementary Figure S4 newly includes ANTs and KeyMorph in a qualitative localization comparison; v1's qualitative Figure 2 showed only the proposed method against ground truth.

E3.justification: New protocols include SVM classification with F1 evaluation and 10-fold cross-validation on 210 PPMI scans for PD and 114 PPMI/ADNI scans for AD, plus a 30-versus-30 biomarker comparison. Section 4.5 also stratifies existing test results into three age groups. Original detector training and benchmark settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds an age-stratified analysis under the existing ICBM152 atlas, reports non-convergence when using either consistency sub-loss alone, and adds the qualitative baseline case in Figure S4. Existing component, rotation, and kernel-size analyses remain. Alternative atlases are proposed for future study, not actually tested.

E5.justification: v2 adds an age-group ANOVA, Wilcoxon tests with Bonferroni correction across 496 distances, and F1 means with reported variability alongside 10-fold cross-validation. Existing benchmark uncertainty reporting and paired t-tests remain unchanged. No additional detector training runs or seeds are documented.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain all numerical results, and Figure 3 retains its curves. Newly reported findings include age-group MREs, single-loss non-convergence, 117 of 496 significantly differing PD-related distances, and classification F1 scores of 81.2 ± 8.8% for PD and 93.5 ± 6.3% for AD. Figure S4 adds qualitative comparative results.

T1.justification: The method equations (1)–(8) and supplementary TPS definitions, constraints, derivation, and regularization equations (S1)–(S6) are unchanged. The new triangular-consistency explanation introduces no formal result or proof.

C1.justification: The title, abstract, first contribution, and conclusion narrow the framing from medical/anatomical landmarks to brain landmarks. A new contribution asserts clinical applicability in exploratory neurological diagnosis. The central single-atlas, consistency-learning, and contrast-generalization claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 introduces a triangular explanation for the consistency terms, interprets the age ANOVA as supporting robustness despite a young-adult atlas, and interprets downstream findings as supporting PD/AD diagnosis. It explicitly defers alternative-atlas testing. Existing limitations concerning global registration accuracy and computationally constrained batch size remain.

D1.justification: The supplement adds the PPMI acquisition date and identifier and an ADNI access acknowledgment. Conversely, v2 removes v1's future public-code-release statement and repository link. This establishes removal of access information, not that an existing repository became unavailable. Core implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds ADNI and PPMI references and four works on landmark-based brain disease diagnosis, extending the application positioning. It removes Zhong et al.'s cephalogram landmark-detection reference. The related-work subsections and central methodological positioning otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 consolidates the introduction around three challenges, shortens and rearranges the discussion, renames CAMLD to CABLD, and adds descriptive ablation headings and downstream-task sections. Most methodological prose and the overall main-section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure S4, adjusts diagram callouts and Figure 3 labeling, and changes Tables 1–2 to use an Optimization Metric heading and green highlighting. Figure 2's caption clarifies projection-based visualization. Existing supplementary figures are retained but grouped onto later pages.

improvement.justification: v2 provides clearer brain-specific framing and useful additional analyses while preserving the core evidence. However, its AD classification and initial PD biomarker comparison confound diagnosis with dataset source, without reported controls separating those effects. The single-atlas age ANOVA (p = 0.07) also does not establish template-choice robustness, despite the interpretation in Section 4.5. Removal of the code-release link reduces access information. These benefits and weaknesses leave the net quality change uncertain.
